Critical data gaps

Promoter ↔ store mappingNeeded to attribute store outcomes to individuals.
Weekly store-level funnelNeeded to locate the exact conversion constraint.
Store referral countNeeded to test store-team contribution.
Reason-coded objectionsNeeded to quantify price/privacy/prescription/use-case barriers.
Return-visit outcomesNeeded to test availability-related missed sales.
Recruitment source × productivityNeeded to evaluate recruitment quality beyond closure speed.
Comparable store baselineNeeded to isolate program effects from store context.

Questions before changing the model

  1. Where exactly is the funnel leaking at each store?
  2. Are low-demo stores capacity constrained or referral constrained?
  3. Are high-demo/low-conversion stores facing objection or qualification issues?
  4. Which promoter practices are associated with higher conversion?
  5. Does store format explain differences, or do exceptions exist?
  6. Which customer objections recur most often?
  7. What happens when store staff actively refer customers?
MASTER OPERATIONAL STRATEGY · FULL SOURCE PLAYBOOK
Strategy Playbook
The complete strategy architecture: diagnostic verdict, analytical priorities, six execution pillars, detailed interventions, prescription proposition, 90-day milestones and target KPIs.
31 STORES · 48 POSITIONS · 6 PILLARS
PLAYBOOK SCOPE: This section intentionally preserves the strategy document's proposed targets, mechanics and terminology. Proposed targets are shown as playbook targets; they are not presented as already-achieved case results.

1 · Program overview & diagnostic verdict

What the strategy document says the operation must solve
Operating footprint

31 stores · 48 approved promoter positions

Promoters are deployed across Premium Malls, High Street Opticians and Consumer Electronics outlets to drive product awareness, live demonstrations and unit sales.

  • Top-line volume in the playbook: 92 units sold in Week 1 → 111 in Week 6.
  • Demo volume: 1,184 in Week 1 → 1,476 in Week 6.
  • The playbook frames the issue as moving from assisted-sales activity toward category building.
Diagnostic verdict

Activity is scaling; category-building mechanisms need strengthening

According to the playbook, category building requires clearer daily utility, point-of-sale app activation, sticky optical-staff referral loops and stronger customer retention.

Core friction points
  • ~7.5% overall demo-to-sale conversion in the playbook.
  • Channel performance disparity between High Street optical stores and Premium Malls.
  • Promoter productivity varies by recruitment background.
  • More than 20% of buyers are described as leaving without companion-app pairing/activation.
  • Regular store staff are described as treating promoters as third-party vendors, limiting referrals.
  • Management coverage is described as missing 9–13 store visits weekly.

3 · The six execution pillars

Complete strategy architecture
01

Adaptive & Localized Pitching

Replace generic corporate spec sheets with three modular, scenario-based demos tailored to store format and regional customer profile.

Open full playbook

High Street Opticians: prescription wearers / frame buyers → prescription & everyday utility, frame ergonomics, prescription compatibility, open-ear commuting audio.

Premium Malls: lifestyle/fashion shoppers and travelers → hands-free photo/video capture, instant social sharing and styling.

Tech Hubs: tech enthusiasts / early adopters → Meta AI & productivity, hands-free voice commands, visual translation and AI queries.

Qualifying question: “Are you looking for everyday prescription/sunglass utility, or hands-free technology for travel and daily capture?”

02

White-Glove POS Setup & Retention Nudges

Eliminate the activation gap with a 5-minute concierge setup before checkout, followed by a 14-day feature drip.

Open full playbook

Checkout checklist: pair Meta View; configure default voice controls; take a test photo/video and transfer it live; play a 10-second open-ear audio track.

Day 1: hands-free photo trial. Day 3: voice assistance during commutes. Day 7: hands-free WhatsApp/Instagram video calls. Day 10: custom touch-control shortcuts.

Usage trigger: if no AI query occurs in 3 days, send the specified Meta AI discovery nudge.

03

Real-Time Dynamic Performance Dashboard

Replace static weekly review packs with store-level tracking and action triggers.

Open full playbook

Conversion quality: demos → enquiries → units sold; retrain if conversion drops below 8%.

POS activation: % of sold units paired before leaving; alert if activation falls below 90%.

Promoter productivity: sales yield per active hour/day; adjust shifts when low-traffic hours waste time.

Store referrals: leads passed by optical staff; run a 5-minute morning refresher if referrals hit zero.

04

Immediate Sales Acceleration Levers

Change incentives, staffing windows, price framing and trial access to attack conversion friction.

Open full playbook

Incentives: 1.5× commission multiplier for promoters above 12% conversion; ₹200–₹300 micro-bonus for successful store-optician referrals.

Peak shifts: Thursday–Sunday, 3 PM–9 PM; temporary dual coverage during high-volume High Street weekend rushes.

Purchase friction: no-cost EMI framing and immediate vision testing with host opticians when prescription questions arise.

VIP trials: 3-km geotargeted Instagram ads offering 10-minute reserved VIP trials via WhatsApp.

05

Social Media Content & O2O Analytics

Connect short-form digital content to physical store visits through trackable geo-targeted CTAs.

Open full playbook

Flow: Social Media Byte → UTM-tracked CTA → geofenced VIP WhatsApp booking → in-store QR scan → POS sale & app pairing.

Customer interactions: 15–30 sec first-impression reactions → VIP trial booking.

POV: “A Day Through My Glasses” → deep-link to store locator.

Expert: optician / tech insights → appointment calendar.

Demo bytes: 15-second feature micro-tutorials → geofenced in-store demo coupon.

06

Complimentary Single-Vision Prescription Lens Program

Use a prescription-led value proposition to address lens-cost and fitting friction in optical channels.

Open full playbook

Offer: Buy Ray-Ban Meta Smart Glasses + complimentary single-vision prescription lenses + free eye checkup.

Lens scope: Index 1.56/1.60 with Anti-Reflective & Blue Light coating; flat credit such as ₹2,500 toward Progressive/Transitions upgrades.

Economics stated in the document: lens wholesale production cost represented as <10–15% of retail price.

4 · People capability engine

Peer-to-peer learning from proven selling behaviour
Proposed intervention · People Lab

Peer-to-Peer Promoter Academy / Champion Promoter Program

Use consistently strong promoters as internal trainers. Identify Champions from repeatable performance, codify their selling behaviours, train peers through short role-play sessions, then measure the coached promoter's improvement.

  • Champion selection: consistent sales, conversion, customer feedback, product knowledge, attendance and ability to articulate their method.
  • Training: customer opening, qualification, contextual demos, objection handling, closing and store-team referrals.
  • Measurement: compare baseline vs 2-week and 30-day unit productivity and conversion.
  • Scale: convert proven behaviours into onboarding and the category expansion playbook.

Operating principle

Build the category, not just the activity

The strategy links demand generation, contextual selling, purchase-friction removal, post-purchase activation, store-team referrals, promoter productivity and allocation decisions into one operating system.

PEOPLE ENGINE · INTERNAL KNOWLEDGE TRANSFER
Promoter Champions Academy
Turn the strongest promoters' practical selling experience into a repeatable peer-learning system — so capability scales inside the network, not only through central training.
PROPOSED INTERVENTION
IDENTIFY → CODIFY → TEACH → PRACTICE → MEASURE → REPEAT

Make your best promoters force multipliers.

Select consistently strong performers, capture what they actually do differently, convert those behaviours into short peer-training modules, and measure whether coached promoters improve.

IDENTIFYHigh & consistent performers
→
CODIFYWinning behaviours
→
COACHPeer sessions
→
MEASURE2-week / 30-day lift

Who becomes a Champion?

Selection should use a balanced scorecard rather than one strong week of sales.

  • Consistent unit sales and demo-to-sale conversion
  • Strong enquiry handling and customer feedback
  • High product knowledge / training performance
  • Reliable attendance and store discipline
  • Ability to explain the “why” behind their selling approach
CHAMPIONTrains 2–3 peers, shares best practices and runs role-play sessions.
COACHED PROMOTERPractices the method, receives shadowing and tracks improvement.
MANAGERValidates the method, observes sessions and monitors performance lift.
PROGRAM TEAMCodifies repeatable practices into the promoter playbook.

What gets taught?

  • Opening: how to approach different customer types.
  • Qualification: identify lifestyle, technology and prescription intent.
  • Demo: make the customer experience the benefit instead of feature-dumping.
  • Objection handling: price, phone comparison, “why do I need it?”, prescription and privacy.
  • Closing: recognise purchase intent and move enquiry → sale.
  • Store collaboration: build referrals from optical/store staff.

Peer-learning operating loop

→
2 · CODIFYCapture their repeatable behaviours and scripts.
→
3 · TEACH30-minute peer session + role-play.
→

→

→
6 · SCALEPromote successful behaviours into the playbook.
PRIMARYUnit liftChange in weekly units for coached promoters vs baseline.
QUALITYConversion liftChange in demo → sale conversion after coaching.
BEHAVIOURDemo qualityObserved use of qualifying, contextual demo and objection handling.
SCALEChampion yieldNumber of peers improved per Champion.
90-DAY INTEGRATION

Days 1–15: identify Champion candidates and document winning behaviours. Days 16–45: launch peer sessions and shadowing. Days 46–60: compare coached vs baseline performance and refine modules. Days 61–90: institutionalise the strongest modules in onboarding and the category expansion playbook.

Intervention library

Proposed tests derived from case evidence and hypotheses
01 · Conversion

Use-case-led demo

Test whether a more structured customer journey improves engagement and conversion where category/use-case clarity is a suspected friction.

Primary: Demo → enquiry
Secondary: Demo → sale
Data: Store × promoter × week × funnel
What changes?

Identify → qualify → demonstrate → resolve concern → conversion ask. Keep the product and core program unchanged.

02 · Objections

Objection-handling playbook

Test consistent responses to objections explicitly surfaced in the case, including price, privacy, prescription and comparison concerns.

Primary: Enquiry → sale
Secondary: Demo → sale
Data: Reason-coded objections
What changes?

Record objection type, apply a consistent response structure and compare conversion against baseline.

03 · Store execution

Store-team referral

Test whether concise store-team enablement increases qualified customer opportunities reaching the promoter.

Primary: Store referrals
Secondary: Referral → demo / sale
Data: Referral source
What changes?

Brief store staff on what the product is, who to refer and how to hand over the customer.

04 · Availability

Promoter availability

Test whether missed interactions or return visits create measurable conversion leakage in stores where this issue appears.

Primary: Return-visit conversion
Secondary: Complaints
Data: Availability / return outcome
What changes?

Capture missed interactions and subsequent outcomes rather than assuming availability is the cause.

05 · Demand generation

Social → Store O2O

Test whether short-form use-case content plus a geo-targeted booking CTA generates higher-intent store visits and measurable downstream sales.

Primary: Booked trial → show-up
Secondary: Trial → sale
Data: UTM / booking / store outcome
What changes?

Customer reaction, POV and expert content route into a reserved in-store trial. Judge the full path, not views alone.

06 · Purchase friction

Prescription lens proposition

Test a complimentary single-vision prescription lens + eye-check proposition where prescription compatibility is a recurring customer question.

Primary: Eligible buyer → sale
Secondary: Redemption / activation
Data: Eligibility / offer / purchase
What changes?

Run the proposition in selected optical stores. Validate customer response and unit economics before considering scale.

INTERVENTION RULE

One diagnosed problem → one targeted intervention → one primary KPI → one decision. The interventions are proposed tests, not established causal explanations.

Growth engine pilots

Two interventions plugged into the customer funnel
TOP OF FUNNEL · SOCIAL → STORE

O2O content-to-trial pilot

Run customer-reaction, POV and expert content with a geo-targeted CTA that routes customers to a reserved 10-minute in-store trial.

Content→CTA→WhatsApp→Trial→Sale
Primary: booked trials and show-up rate
Secondary: trial → demo → sale, revenue per booked trial
CONTROLLED PILOT · DO NOT ASSUME CAUSALITY
CONVERSION · PRESCRIPTION

Prescription lens proposition

Test a complimentary single-vision prescription lens + eye-check proposition in selected optical stores. Treat the offer as a hypothesis, not an established solution.

Eligible buyer→Offer→Redemption→Purchase→Activation
Primary: eligible-buyer → purchase conversion
Secondary: offer redemption, app activation, complaints, unit economics
CONTROLLED PILOT · ECONOMICS VALIDATION REQUIRED

WHY THESE BELONG IN THE SAME PLAN

Social O2O addresses demand quality before the store visit. The prescription proposition addresses a specific purchase friction after customer engagement. Both must be measured through the same funnel rather than judged on impressions or offer uptake alone.

Should we add more promoters?

Decision tree

Capacity should follow evidence

STEP 01Is activity low relative to the store's context?
→
STEP 02Is conversion also low, or is the existing selling execution strong?
LOW ACTIVITY
Investigate availability, store referrals and capacity before assuming headcount is the answer.
HIGH ACTIVITY + LOW CONVERSION
Investigate qualification, objections and demo-to-sale execution before adding capacity.
STRONG ACTIVITY + STRONG CONVERSION
If activity remains constrained despite strong execution, capacity becomes a testable option.

COMPETITION MODE · 5-SLIDE RECOMMENDATION

From activity to repeatable store performance.

Five slides tell the management story. Every slide links back to the underlying evidence in the control tower.

THE STORY IN ONE LINE Activity is growing → store performance varies → the mechanism is not yet linked → diagnose → pilot → scale.
01 · WHAT IS HAPPENING?

The program is scaling activity — but the category-building question remains unresolved.

The program is generating meaningful customer activity and commercial output, but store-level performance is heterogeneous and the current data does not explain why.

THE MANAGEMENT QUESTION

“We have people in the stores, but are we actually building the category?”

Growth in activity is encouraging, but it does not by itself establish that the assisted-selling model is consistently converting customer interaction into category adoption.

02 · WHERE IS THE PROBLEM?

The constraint is not uniform: stores appear to face different funnel situations.

The displayed store rows show different combinations of activity intensity and demo-to-sale conversion. That argues for targeted diagnosis rather than one intervention for every store.

03 · WHAT DO WE NEED TO KNOW?

The current data shows the outcome — but not the mechanism.

We have useful program, store, promoter and customer-voice data. The missing layer is the linked Promoter → Store → Week → Customer Funnel.

WHAT WE KNOW
  • Program: weekly activity, units, revenue, enquiries, activations, attendance, training
  • Store: footfall, presence, demonstrations, enquiries, units, ASP, rating
  • Promoter: tenure, category, training, attendance, demos, units, incentive
  • Customer voice: clarity, price, privacy, prescription, referrals, availability and demo feedback
WHAT WE DON'T KNOW
Promoter

Funnel
  • Which promoter practices drive conversion?
  • Which store practices drive referrals?
  • Which objections explain lost sales?
  • Which stores are genuinely capacity constrained?
01Promoter × store mapping 02Weekly store funnel 03Reason-coded objections 04Store referral tracking 05Return-visit outcomes 06Recruitment source × productivity
Recommendation: Before structural changes, build the evidence layer that connects deployment to conversion.
04 · WHAT SHOULD WE DO IN THE NEXT 90 DAYS?

Diagnose → Pilot → Scale

Use the first 30 days to locate the constraint, the next 30 to test targeted interventions, and the final 30 to institutionalise what the evidence supports.

01DAYS 1–30

DIAGNOSE

Build the missing evidence layer
  • Promoter × store × week dataset
  • Store-level funnel
  • Customer feedback coding
  • Activity × conversion segmentation
  • Priority constraints
OUTPUT
Store diagnostic profiles + pilot design
02DAYS 31–60

PILOT

Test interventions against specific constraints
  • Use-case-led demonstrations
  • Objection-handling playbook
  • Store-team referral enablement
  • Promoter availability discipline
OUTPUT
Evidence on intervention effectiveness
03DAYS 61–90

SCALE

Institutionalise what works
  • Compare pilot vs baseline
  • Replicate validated practices
  • Build operating playbooks
  • Establish weekly funnel dashboard
  • Evaluate capacity only where justified
OUTPUT
Standard operating model + capacity recommendation

GROWTH ENGINE A · DEMAND GENERATION

Social → Store O2O

Use short-form, use-case-led content to create higher-intent store visits rather than relying only on casual in-store discovery.

15–30s content→Geo CTA→WhatsApp booking→10-min trial→Store sale
Measure: CTA clicks → bookings → show-up → demo → sale → revenue. PILOT IN SELECTED STORES
GROWTH ENGINE B · PURCHASE FRICTION

Prescription Lens Proposition

Test a complimentary single-vision prescription lens + eye-check proposition in selected optical stores where prescription questions recur.

Prescription need→Offer→Eye check→Purchase→Activation
Measure: Eligible buyers → offer acceptance → redemption → purchase conversion. PILOT · ECONOMICS TO BE VALIDATED

INTEGRATED CATEGORY-BUILDING FUNNEL

The two ideas sit at different points in the same system: social media improves the quality of demand entering the funnel; the prescription proposition tests a specific conversion barrier in optical stores.
